walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1796 Edward Jenner noticed milkmaids who caught cowpox did not get smallpox.

He tested the idea on James Phipps and published his findings in 1798. In 1853 vaccination was made compulsory for babies.

In 1854 John Snow mapped cholera deaths around the Broad Street pump in Soho.

He removed the pump handle and deaths fell. In 1861 Louis Pasteur published Germ Theory — proving microbes, not miasma, cause disease.

In 1867 Joseph Lister used carbolic acid spray in surgery — deaths from infection plummeted.

Florence Nightingale's hygiene reforms cut hospital death rates. Parliament passed the 1875 Public Health Act, forcing councils to provide clean water and sewers.

options: Cholera
Smallpox
Polio
Tuberculosis

mcqs.q: What chemical did Lister use as an antiseptic?
options: Penicillin
Carbolic acid
Chloroform
Iodine

mcqs.q: Why did public health reforms accelerate after 1848?
options: The 1848 Public Health Act followed cholera epidemics and Chadwick's report; John Snow's 1854 Broad Street pump study reinforced the case for clean water by 1875.
The 1875 Act made the NHS free for all workers.
The 1832 Reform Act allowed women to vote for the first time.
Public health acts were passed because Victorians discovered germs in the 1840s.

mcqs.q: Why were 19th-century industrial cities so unhealthy?
options: The 1832 Reform Act allowed women to vote for the first time.
Rapid population growth outpaced housing, water and sewage; lack of regulation produced overcrowded slums and cholera epidemics until reforms followed Chadwick's 1842 report.
Cities were unhealthy because factory smoke poisoned the food.
Cities were unhealthy because Victorians did not care about hygiene.
